parts.visual:
A founder says: 'We made $500,000 this month!' The VC asks: 'How much of that is MRR?' The founder replies: 'Only $50,000. The rest was a one-time consulting fee.' The VC loses all interest.

The Metrics:
1. MRR (Monthly Recurring Revenue): The total amount of predictable, subscription-based revenue a company generates every single month.
2. ARR (Annual Recurring Revenue): MRR multiplied by 12. It is the annualized run-rate of the business.
parts.audio: In a SaaS company, one-time revenue does not matter. The entire valuation of the company is mathematically tied to the growth of MRR. It is the absolute most important number on your dashboard.

questions.question: A startup has 1,000 customers paying $50 per month. They also sold a $10,000 customized server to one client this month. What is their MRR?
options: $50,000. (1,000 customers * $50). The $10,000 server sale is 'Non-Recurring Revenue' and must be strictly separated from the MRR calculation.
questions.correct_answer: $50,000. (1,000 customers * $50). The $10,000 server sale is 'Non-Recurring Revenue' and must be strictly separated from the MRR calculation.
questions.explanation: Never mix services revenue with subscription revenue when talking to investors.

questions.question: Listen to the financial report. What is 'Expansion MRR'?
questions.tts_text: Our base MRR remained the same, but our Expansion MRR grew by 15% because our existing users upgraded to the 'Premium' tier and bought extra user licenses.
options: Additional recurring revenue generated from existing customers. This is highly profitable because you don't have to pay marketing costs to acquire these upgrades.
questions.correct_answer: Additional recurring revenue generated from existing customers. This is highly profitable because you don't have to pay marketing costs to acquire these upgrades.
questions.explanation: Expansion MRR is the secret engine of a massively successful SaaS business.

questions.question: If a startup has an MRR of $100,000, what is their ARR?
options: $1,200,000. ARR is simply MRR multiplied by 12. It represents what the company will make in the next year if everything stays exactly the same.
questions.correct_answer: $1,200,000. ARR is simply MRR multiplied by 12. It represents what the company will make in the next year if everything stays exactly the same.
questions.explanation: Most investors value startups as a 'Multiple of ARR' (e.g., valuing the company at 10x its ARR).

questions.question: What is 'Contraction MRR'?
options: When the company shrinks the office.
When an existing customer decides to 'downgrade' their subscription to a cheaper plan. They didn't churn (cancel completely), but they are paying you less money than before.
questions.correct_answer: When an existing customer decides to 'downgrade' their subscription to a cheaper plan. They didn't churn (cancel completely), but they are paying you less money than before.
questions.explanation: Net MRR Growth = (New MRR + Expansion MRR) - (Churn MRR + Contraction MRR).

questions.question: Order the words to describe SaaS valuation:
questions.explanation: The higher the predictability, the higher the valuation multiple.
